Verbovets Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Verbovets once had a population that was more than half Jewish — 1,934 of a recorded population that also included 1,144 Orthodox Christians and 583 Catholics — before the town was totally devastated during the Khmelnytsky rebellion of 1648–1654, a blow from which its Jewish population never fully recovered, falling to just 118 people by 1787. The community partially rebuilt over the following century, reaching 661 by 1897, but had dwindled to only 165 by 1926. All of Verbovets's remaining Jews were shot shortly after Hungarian and then German forces occupied the town in July 1941.
